title: Realization preserves homotopy equivalences of Reedy-cofibrant simplicial objects
statement:
Use simplicial model categories as defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], simplicial tensors of [def-coef-simplicial-tensor-cotensor], the Reedy model structure of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure], and combinatorial simplicial homotopies as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-extra-degeneracy-prism]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a simplicial model category, and let $A_\bullet,B_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal M$ be Reedy-cofibrant simplicial objects. Define the tensor realization of any simplicial object $C_\bullet$ by
$$|C_\bullet|=\operatorname{coeq}\left(\coprod_{\alpha:[m]\to[n]}C_n\otimes\Delta^m\rightrightarrows\coprod_{n\geq0}C_n\otimes\Delta^n\right),$$
where $\Delta^n=\operatorname{Hom}_\Delta(-,[n])$ and the arrows are induced respectively by $C(\alpha)$ and $\Delta^\alpha$. Suppose $f:A_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ has a map $g:B_\bullet\to A_\bullet$, a combinatorial simplicial homotopy connecting $gf$ and $1_A$, and a combinatorial simplicial homotopy connecting $fg$ and $1_B$, each in either orientation. Then $|f|:|A_\bullet|\to|B_\bullet|$ is a weak equivalence in $\mathcal M$. No fibrancy hypothesis is imposed. Here a combinatorial simplicial homotopy consists of degree-raising prism maps; it does not mean a degreewise family $A_n\otimes\Delta^1\to B_n$.

source.place: Dugger, A Primer on Homotopy Colimits, coend realization (3.2), skeletal pushout in the proof of Theorem 3.5 (printed pp.9-10), and simplicial tensor/SM7 in Section 19.1 (printed p.90); the explicit general combinatorial-homotopy formulation and its proof are supplied by the second reader in report.md, not asserted to be a verbatim numbered theorem of Dugger. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: The coequalizer formula defines a functor from simplicial objects to $\mathcal M$: a map of simplicial objects induces maps on every coproduct summand, and naturality makes them respect both coend relations. The identity map and a composite map act summandwise as identities and composites, so $|1_C|=1_{|C|}$ and $|g\circ f|=|g|\circ|f|$. This is an elementary coend calculation using the chosen tensors.

source.place: coend realization (3.2), printed p. 9; functoriality of the coend quotient is written out here

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-reedy-realization-prism] with $X_\bullet=Y_\bullet=A_\bullet$ to the given combinatorial homotopy connecting $gf$ and $1_A$. It gives a cylinder $P_A=|A_\bullet|\otimes\Delta^1$ and a map $P_A\to |A_\bullet|$ whose restrictions to the two vertex maps are $|g||f|$ and $1_{|A_\bullet|}$. If the input homotopy has the opposite orientation these restrictions occur in the opposite order; retain that order, since the endpoint argument below treats the two vertices symmetrically.

source.place: Agent-written combinatorial prism transfer; compare Dugger formula (3.2), Theorem 3.5 skeletal pushout (printed pp.10-11), and Section 19.1. The source does not state this exact transfer.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-reedy-realization-prism] with $X_\bullet=Y_\bullet=B_\bullet$ to the other homotopy. It gives a cylinder $P_B=|B_\bullet|\otimes\Delta^1$ and a map $P_B\to |B_\bullet|$ with endpoint restrictions $|f||g|$ and $1_{|B_\bullet|}$, in one of the two orders. Both applications have Reedy-cofibrant source and target, because the item assumes this for $A_\bullet$ and $B_\bullet$.

source.place: Agent-written combinatorial prism transfer; compare Dugger formula (3.2), Theorem 3.5 skeletal pushout (printed pp.10-11), and Section 19.1. The source does not state this exact transfer.

proof.text: Here is the endpoint calculation, using two-out-of-three from [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization]. In either cylinder $p:P\to Z$, each vertex inclusion $i_j$ is a weak equivalence since $p i_j=1_Z$ and $p$ is a weak equivalence. For the map $H:P\to Z$ supplied in Steps 2 or 3, one composite $H i_j$ is $1_Z$, so two-out-of-three makes $H$ a weak equivalence; then the other composite $H i_{1-j}$ is a weak equivalence as a composite of weak equivalences. Therefore $|g||f|$ and $|f||g|$ are weak equivalences. Identities are weak equivalences because they belong to both lifting classes, hence to their intersections with $W$, in the two weak factorization systems. This uses no fibrancy assumption.

source.place: Cylinder.LeftHomotopy.weakEquivalence_iff, lines 140-145; elementary two-out-of-three proof written explicitly here rather than made into a node.

proof.text: Use the ordinary localization $\gamma:\mathcal M\to\mathcal H$ at weak equivalences, in an enlarged universe, and [lem-coef-model-localization-detects-weak-equivalences]. Write $F=\gamma(|f|)$ and $G=\gamma(|g|)$. Step 4 implies that $GF$ and $FG$ are isomorphisms. The map $L=(GF)^{-1}G$ is a left inverse of $F$ and $R=G(FG)^{-1}$ is a right inverse. Thus $L=L(FR)=(LF)R=R$, and $F$ is an isomorphism. The cited detection statement now implies that $|f|$ is a weak equivalence. Its model-category hypothesis is exactly that of the item, its required universes may be enlarged, and it assumes neither endpoint cofibrant nor fibrant.

source.place: Theorem 1.2.10(iv), printed p.13, via the existing localization-detection node; the two inverse formulas are written out here.
